ledger.x: 'they took Achaea and Elis, and after defeating the local Greeks' at Koundouros; Patras and Andravida 'fell without struggle'; Pontikon, Coron and Kalamata taken.

Boniface broke the Isthmus line; 'by spring 1205 he controlled the countryside of the northeastern Peloponnese, while the fortified cities held out'; Acrocorinth blockaded 'in a siege that was to last five years'.
Treaty of Sapienza, June 1209: Venice kept 'Modon and Coron' and recognised Villehardouin in the rest of the peninsula; he 'became a vassal of the Republic' (nominal).
Sgouros died 1208; 'Resistance was continued by a certain Theodore [Komnenos Doukas], but in the end, the citadel fell in 1210'.
Argos and Nauplia held two more years but the organised resistance ended with Acrocorinth.
'Nauplia and then Argos fell in 1212' (conquest 1211-1212); the garrisons were Sgouros' heirs under Theodore Doukas.
The cities 'were granted as a fief to' Otto de la Roche 'by Geoffrey I of Villehardouin, prince of Achaea'; Guy I 'owed homage to the prince of Achaea' for Thebes and Argos.
Monemvasia 'capitulated only in 1248' after a three-year siege; the self-governing town was under no state.
Baldwin II transferred the suzerainty over the Duchy of the Archipelago to William II in 1248; it passed to the Angevins with the principality in 1278.
'These castles secured the Frankish control of the Mount Taygetus'.
Infobox: Mystras capital 1249-1261.
War of the Euboeote Succession 1256-1258: William claimed the northern terziere (1255); in June 1256 'the two triarchs rejected Achaean overlordship and swore fealty to Venice'.
Guy I of Athens led the barons against William; Salona and Bodonitsa joined him, Genoa backed William.
Karydi, May/June 1258: Guy defeated, 'subsequently besieged in Thebes and forced to surrender'; judged by the High Court at Nikli, pardoned by Louis IX.
Fighting ended at Karydi; 'a definitive peace treaty was not concluded until 1262', restoring the status quo with the triarchs' allegiance to William.
Battle of Pelagonia, 1259: 'the Nicaeans inflicted a decisive defeat on the Franks'; William 'was captured and sent to Nicaea'.
Pelagonia
Treaty of 1262: 'The triarchs recognized William's overlordship, and Venice kept some of its gains'.
William's ransom, agreed late 1261: 'the cession of Monemvasia, Grand Magne, and Mystras'; 'The handover was effected in 1262' (early 1262, Prinitza page).
Seat back to Andravida after the cession of Mystras.
'By the end of 1262, they seized Cape Maleas and took control of the nearby Mani Peninsula.'
Summer 1263: Constantine Palaiologos marched 'up the rivers Eurotas and Alfeios towards the Achaean capital, Andravida'; routed at Prinitza (1263) and Makryplagi (1263/64).
'By 1264, only Lacedaemon appears to have remained in Frankish hands in the region'; William 'repopulated and fortified the old city of Sparta' after Makryplagi, lost later in the decade (undated).
'The conflict degenerated into skirmishes on both sides before being suspended entirely'; no treaty.
With Charles I as prince the Archipelago's homage went to the Angevin crown directly.
Bookkeeping end: the triarchs' overlord became Charles of Anjou as prince (and in practice Venice); Licario's Byzantine conquest of most of Euboea (1276-c.1280) also intervened.

William II died 1 May 1278; 'Charles succeeded him without opposition' under the Treaty of Viterbo (24/27 May 1267) and ruled through the bailli Galeran of Ivry: the Villehardouin principality becomes an Angevin possession, same state, same colour (rule 2).
Charles II 'granted the Principality to Isabelle of Villehardouin upon her marriage with Florent of Hainaut' (1289): Villehardouin-Hainaut princes under Angevin suzerainty.
Ferdinand of Majorca 'seized Clarenza in June 1315 and briefly took control of the Morea' as rival prince; the Catalan Company's aid from Athens 'was tardy'.
Matilda and Louis of Burgundy 'returned to the Morea in the spring of 1316 with Venetian aid'; Ferdinand 'was killed at the Battle of Manolada, near Glarentza, on 5 July 1316'.

'In 1320, Karytaina and the eastern half of the ancient barony fell into the hands of the Byzantines under Andronikos Asen'; Akova 'along with the castles of Karytaina... fell to the Byzantines' the same year.
Corinth, mortgaged to Nerio Acciaioli by Angelo Acciaioli after 1365 and 'confirmed' as hereditary in 1371 by Philip of Taranto; the Pope called Nerio 'lord of the town of Corinth' in November 1372.

'In 1383, Achaea was annexed by Charles III of Naples' and 'the Vicary government began' under the Navarrese Company (entered the Morea 1378), 'the reigning power in Frankish Greece'; princely rights sold to Pedro de San Superano 1396.

Maria of Enghien 'sold the two cities to Venice' (1388); 'Before Venice could take possession, Argos was seized by the Despot Theodore I Palaiologos' and Nerio took Nauplia; Nauplia soon Venetian, Argos handed to Venice 1394.
'Centurione purchased the rights of the title of Prince of Achaea by Ladislaus of Naples in 1404': the Zaccaria principality.
'Leonardo and Carlo conquered Glarentza in 1408'.

ledger.x: Centurione 'was able to retake Glarentza and expel the Toccos' (1414).
ledger.cpn: County Palatine of Cephalonia and Zakynthos (Tocco)

ledger.x: Invasion of 1417 'led by the despot Theodore II Palaeologus and Emperor John VIII'.
'They took Messenia and Elis and holed up Centurione in Glarentza, from which he fled by sea in the spring of 1418'; Kyparissia (Arcadia) and Chalandritsa remained his.

'In 1418, Olivier Franco, a former captain of the Toccos seized Glarentza'; 'in 1421 Olivier sold Glarentza to Carlo Tocco' (the despotate-of-epirus dossier records the 1421 gain with counterpart principality-of-achaea, the nominal owner).
Theodore II 'attacked Centurione and defeated him in battle' (undated, after 1417).
Seat at Chalandritsa after the loss of Andravida and Glarentza.

'The prince resisted for some time but eventually he surrendered'; by the treaty Thomas married Catherine Zaccaria (1430, at Mystras) and became heir; 'Centurione was allowed to keep his inheritance, the barony of Arcadia'.
Centurione 'retired to Arcadia in 1430'; Kyparissia the last seat.
Constantine 'marched towards Patras on 1 March 1429, and they besieged the city on 20 March'; Thomas 'besieged Centurione in Chalandritsa' (1429).
The town accepted Constantine as lord on 4 June 1429; 'Once the Archbishop's castle surrendered to Constantine in July 1430' the Latin archbishopric's temporal lordship ended.
Patras and Chalandritsa
'He died there two years later in 1432.
Infobox 'Dissolved by the Despotate of the Morea: 1432'.

wars.name: Frankish conquest of the Morea
wars.outcome: Frankish conquest; Koundouros summer 1205, Acrocorinth 1210, Nauplia and Argos 1212, Araklovon 1213

wars.name: Siege of Monemvasia
wars.outcome: Capitulation of the town, 1248 (or 1225 per the Monemvasia page)

wars.name: War of the Euboeote Succession
wars.outcome: Achaean victory at Karydi (May/June 1258); peace treaty 1262 restoring the status quo with the triarchs' allegiance to William

wars.name: Pelagonia campaign
wars.outcome: Nicaean victory; William II captured; ransom of Mystras, Grand Magne and Monemvasia (1261/62)

wars.name: Byzantine-Achaean war of 1263-1264
wars.outcome: Achaean victories at Prinitza (1263) and Makryplagi (1263/64); the Byzantines kept most of Laconia; skirmishing then suspended

wars.name: Ferdinand of Majorca's invasion
wars.outcome: Ferdinand killed at Manolada, 5 July 1316; Matilda and Louis of Burgundy restored

wars.name: Tocco-Zaccaria war for Glarentza
wars.outcome: Toccos held Glarentza 1408-1414; Centurione retook it

wars.name: Byzantine conquest of Elis and Messenia
wars.outcome: Theodore II and John VIII took Messenia and Elis; Centurione fled Glarentza by sea, spring 1418

wars.name: Conquest of Patras and Chalandritsa
wars.outcome: Chalandritsa surrendered 1429; Patras castle July 1430; Centurione kept Arcadia until 1432

certainty.note: Conquest and consolidation; the Greek holdouts (Argolid to 1212, Monemvasia to 1248, the Taygetos tribes) and the fief boundaries are approximate.
The Byzantine-Frankish frontier in Arcadia and Skorta moved castle by castle with few dated events (1264, 1320, 1417-18).
